title: Idle Grace Period at Dedicated Chargers — EV Charging Reserved Space
content:
EV charging program terms, Parking License: at a dedicated charger — the charger that comes with an EV Charging Reserved Space — the grace period before idle time is billed on an idle fee line depends on how many other idle fee lines the license has carried in the last 6 months.

## Clause

At a dedicated charger, when no other idle fee line was posted on the license in the 6 months before the handling date, the grace period is 60 minutes; at a dedicated charger, when exactly one other idle fee line was posted on the license in those months, the grace period is 45 minutes; in every other case the grace period is the product's own idle grace period.

"Other" idle fee lines are the license's idle fee lines other than the idle fee line whose idle time is being billed.

## Grace period by case

| Product carries a dedicated charger | Other idle fee lines on the license in the 6 months before the handling date | Grace period |
|---|---|---|
| yes (EV Charging Reserved Space) | none | 60 minutes |
| yes (EV Charging Reserved Space) | exactly one | 45 minutes |
| yes (EV Charging Reserved Space) | two or more | the product's own idle grace period |
| no (any other parking product) | any number | the product's own idle grace period |

## Illustrations (hypothetical lines)

- An EV Charging Reserved Space line records 70 idle minutes, and no other idle fee line was posted on the license in the 6 months before the handling date: the grace period is 60 minutes, leaving 10 billable minutes.
- The same line on a license that carried one other idle fee line 4 months earlier: the grace period is 45 minutes, leaving 25 billable minutes.
- A Structured Garage Space holder's idle line at a shared charger: whatever the history, the grace period is the product's own idle grace period.
